tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

script.description: Self-contained workflow script. Must begin with `export const meta = { name, description, phases }` (pure literal, no computed values) followed by the script body using agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase().

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

description.description: Ignored — set the workflow description in the script's `meta` block.

title.description: Ignored — set the workflow title in the script's `meta` block.

args.description: Optional input value exposed to the script as the global `args`, verbatim. Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — a stringified list breaks `args.filter`/`args.map` in the script. Use for parameterized named workflows (e.g. a research question).

scriptPath.description: Path to a workflow script file on disk. Every Workflow invocation persists its script under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with the same `scriptPath` instead of re-sending the full script. Takes precedence over `script` and `name`.

resumeFromRunId.description: Run ID of a prior Workflow invocation to resume from. Completed agent() calls with unchanged (prompt, opts) return their cached results instantly; only edited or new calls re-run. Same-session only. Stop the prior run first (TaskStop) before resuming.

## After the landing: the coordinator's routing

The coordinator's steps after a landing, in this order, each done whole:

1. The landing report to the curator.
2. The routing: every open row, record default and item for the curator filed with a batch or as a parked line of `PLAN.md`. Each is checked against POSITIONS and the notes `INDEX.md` lists before it is called open, put to the curator or briefed. In the same pass the routing moves out of `PLAN.md` each item the batch built or answered, and any item it finds stale: word for word, into `PLAN-history.md`, under the landing's dated heading and the heading the item stood under. The batch's own line in its phase becomes one line, with its landing commit and its review. An open item whose text also stands in another home (a `review-queue.md` entry, a ledger row, a FACTS or POSITIONS entry) becomes one line in `PLAN.md`: what is asked, its default, and a pointer to that home. No other step takes an item out of `PLAN.md`, which held 519K characters before its consolidation of 2026-10-15, 54 % of them closed (`process-engineering/plan-map.md`, sections 2 and 4).
3. FACTS consolidated as its README says, superseded text moved to `FACTS-history.md`. The commit stage has already written the landed count and distance, and the two stages' seconds (F-53, F-240).
4. The skills, in three moves:
   - One task for the standing skill writer (`tools/skill-writer.sh`, its brief `skill-writer-brief.md`): the batch's revival-change material, the section "Revival changes, for the skill writer" of its `RECORD.md`; the skill sentences that the post-batch review lists as false; and any `skill-touched` item. The writer runs `tools/skills-lint.py` before each commit.
   - A cold read of the parts the writer changed, by an agent given only the skill and `skill-cold-read-brief.md`.
   - The writer fixes the cold read's flags, and the coordinator pushes its commits.
5. The next batch launched only after that, so that its workers read the updated skill (the `coordinator` skill's `references/batch.md`, "The landing").
6. The combined post-batch review, started at the landing, since step 4 takes its list of false skill sentences (the `coordinator` skill's `references/batch.md`, "The landing").

The review explains every new or risen row of the checker count by a named rung edit. It reads the microGPT walk check's result. It reports the batch's measures against the batches before it with `tools/batch-measures.py` on the run's directory (`batch-redesign.md`, "The measures").

## The principle for the batches

Every batch lands with the specification, the library and both paths agreeing. So the work is grouped by what has to change together, not split finer.

Two rules of the batch machinery shape the order: two rungs in one batch may not change the same declaration, and a rung cannot build on another rung of its own batch, since every rung branches from the batch's base (`coordinator/climb-batch-workflow.js:1303`, batch rule 1).

            part, sec, cur = (m.group(1) if m else None), None, None
            continue
        m = re.match(r'### (.*) \((\d+)\)\s*$', ln)
        if m:
            sec = [part, m.group(1), int(m.group(2)), 0]
            sections.append(sec)
            cur = None
            continue
        if ln.startswith('### '):
            sec, cur = None, None
            continue
        start = re.match(r'(\d+)\. ', ln) or re.match(r'- \*\*(\d+)?', ln)
        if sec and start:
            sec[3] += 1
            cur = None
            if start.group(1):
                cur = int(start.group(1))
                items[cur] = [part, sec[1], ln]
        elif cur is not None and ln.startswith('   '):
            items[cur][2] += '\n' + ln
        elif cur is not None and ln.strip():
            cur = None
    return items, sections, lines


def answered(text):
    """{key: text} of the items under (a)'s "Answered by a decision of his"; the key is the item's number, or its bold title."""
    out, inside, key = {}, False, None
    for ln in text.split('\n'):
        if ln.startswith('#'):
            inside, key = ln.startswith(ANSWERED), None
            continue
        if not inside:
            continue
        m = re.match(r'- \*\*(?:Items? )?(\d+)[,.]', ln) or re.match(r'- \*\*(.+?)\*\*', ln)
        if m:
            key = int(m.group(1)) if m.group(1).isdigit() else m.group(1)
            out[key] = ln
        elif key is not None and ln.startswith('  '):
            out[key] += '\n' + ln
        elif ln.strip():
            key = None
    return out


r = subprocess.run(['git', '-C', a.root, 'show', '%s:%s' % (a.base, REL)], capture_output=True, text=True)
if r.returncode:
    sys.exit('queue-check.py: no %s at %s' % (REL, a.base))
old, _, _ = parse(r.stdout)
old_answered = answered(r.stdout)
with open(os.path.join(a.root, REL), encoding='utf-8') as f:
    text_now = f.read()
new, sections, lines = parse(text_now)
fails = {'numbers': [], 'needed': [], 'sections': [], 'head': [], 'answered': []}
for n in sorted(set(old) - set(new)):
    fails['numbers'].append('item %d is gone' % n)
added = sorted(set(new) - set(old))
top = max(old) if old else 0
if added != list(range(top + 1, top + 1 + len(added))):
    fails['numbers'].append('the new numbers %s do not follow %d one by one' % (', '.join(map(str, added)), top))
for n in sorted(new):
    part, theme, text = new[n]
    opened = n in added or (old.get(n, [None])[0] not in ('b', 'c'))
    if part in ('b', 'c') and opened and not re.search(r'^\s*- Needed by:', text, re.M):
        fails['needed'].append('item %d (%s, "%s") has no "Needed by:" line' % (n, part, theme))
for part, theme, count, got in sections:
    if count != got:
        fails['sections'].append('"%s" (%s) counts %d and holds %d' % (theme, part, count, got))
n_b = sum(g for p, t, c, g in sections if p == 'b')
n_c = sum(g for p, t, c, g in sections if p == 'c')
head = [i for i, l in enumerate(lines) if l.startswith('**Counts**') and 'open items' in l]
if len(head) != 1:
    fails['head'].append('%d "**Counts**, N open items" lines' % len(head))
else:
    m = re.search(r'(\d+) open items, (\d+) consequential and (\d+) routine', lines[head[0]])
    if not m or tuple(map(int, m.groups())) != (n_b + n_c, n_b, n_c):
        fails['head'].append('the head says "%s"; the parts hold %d open, %d consequential and %d routine' % (
            m.group(0) if m else lines[head[0]][:80], n_b + n_c, n_b, n_c))
    sums = [0, 0, 0]
    for l in lines[head[0] + 1:]:
        k = re.match(r'- .*: (\d+) \((\d+) consequential, (\d+) routine\)', l)
        if not k:
            break
        sums = [x + int(y) for x, y in zip(sums, k.groups())]
    if sums != [n_b + n_c, n_b, n_c]:
        fails['head'].append('the lines under it add up to %d (%d consequential, %d routine)' % tuple(sums))
for k, text in answered(text_now).items():
    if k in old_answered:
        continue
    body = text.split('Home:')[0]
    why = ['it names a default taken without him ("%s")' % '", "'.join(sorted(set(m.lower() for m in DEFAULT.findall(body))))] if DEFAULT.search(body) else []
    other = sorted({int(n) for n in re.findall(r'\bon item (\d+)', body)} - {k}) if isinstance(k, int) else []
    if other:
        why.append('it cites his word on item %s, not on item %d' % (', '.join(map(str, other)), k))
    if not HIS.search(body):
        why.append('it cites no word of his: no POSITIONS entry, time or answer of his')
    if why:
        fails['answered'].append('item %s, new in "Answered by a decision of his": %s; it stays open in (b) or (c), with its default as landed' % (
            k if isinstance(k, int) else '"%s"' % k[:60], '; '.join(why)))
for k, v in fails.items():
    for x in v:
        print('FAIL %s: %s' % (k, x))
print('queue-check: %d items, %d new (%s); open %d, consequential %d, routine %d; %s' % (
    len(new), len(added), ', '.join(map(str, added)) or 'none', n_b + n_c, n_b, n_c,
    'pass' if not any(fails.values()) else '%d failures' % sum(map(len, fails.values()))))
sys.exit(1 if any(fails.values()) else 0)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""plan-moves.py --root WT --base AT [--stale-at REV]: check that every line taken out of PLAN.md went to PLAN-history.md word for word, and list the PLAN lines that look stale.

A line taken out is a line of PLAN.md at AT, the commit that the worktree WT was made at, that the working
PLAN.md no longer holds, as a whole line: a line moved, cut to a pointer, or changed. Each must stand among
the lines that the working PLAN-history.md gained since AT, as many times as it went. PLAN-history.md only
gains: a line that it lost is a failure too. Blank lines are not counted. Prints the counts, the headings
that PLAN-history.md gained, and each failure; exit 1 on any.

Then, for information only (they never fail), the PLAN lines to look at, one `LOOK` line each with its
reason, read against the working review queue and the history of AT:
  settled   a list line whose own pointer, a sentence "Review-queue item 296.", names items that are each
            settled in the queue's part (a), and that names no item open in (b) or (c); it skips a line that
            already carries a cleanup's mark, "closed at the cleanup of DATE" in any of the queue cleanup's
            forms ("(closed at the cleanup of 2026-11-05: learning)", "item 127, closed at the cleanup of
            2026-11-05: settled", "are closed at the cleanup of 2026-11-05 (learning)"): the cleanup marked
            it in place, and moving it out of PLAN is PLAN's consolidation, not a landing's change
  list      a list line that names three or more items, some of them settled; or one that ties its items
            to a list of the queue's head (the queue's "Needed before the switch-over") and does not name
            the same items
  finding   a line `- Climb batch N's review, finding M ...` whose finding a commit in the history of AT
            names (`batch-N-review.md, finding M`, or "climb batch N's finding M"), where that commit
            changes a file outside the record: a half of the line may be built
With --stale-at REV, it reads PLAN.md and the review queue at REV, and the history of REV, prints only the
LOOK lines, and exits 0: evidence.py gives them to the sorter in plan.md.
"""
import argparse
import collections
import os
import re
import subprocess
import sys

ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
ap.add_argument('--root', required=True)
ap.add_argument('--base', required=True)
ap.add_argument('--stale-at')
a = ap.parse_args()
D = 'explorations/coordinator/'


def at(rel, rev=None):
    rev = rev or a.base
    r = subprocess.run(['git', '-C', a.root, 'show', '%s:%s' % (rev, D + rel)], capture_output=True, text=True)
    if r.returncode:
        sys.exit('plan-moves.py: no %s at %s' % (rel, rev))
    return r.stdout.split('\n')


def now(rel):
    with open(os.path.join(a.root, D + rel), encoding='utf-8') as f:
        return f.read().split('\n')


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- the PLAN lines to look at

ITEMS = re.compile(r'[Rr]eview-queue items? (\d+(?:(?:,\s*|,? and |,? or )\d+)*)')
OWN = re.compile(r'(?:^\s*- |[.;]\s+)Review-queue items? (\d+(?:(?:,\s*|,? and |,? or )\d+)*)')
CLEANUP_MARK = re.compile(r'\bclosed at the cleanup of \d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}\b')
HEAD_LIST = re.compile(r'\*\*([^*]+?):\*\*\s*(\d[\d,\s]*)')
FINDING_LINE = re.compile(r"\s*- [Cc]limb batch (\w+)'s review, finding (\d+)\b")
RECORD = re.compile(r'explorations/(coordinator/(PLAN|PLAN-history|review-queue|INDEX|FACTS|POSITIONS|FACTS-history|POSITIONS-history|BOOT|HELD)\.md$|reviews/|fortress-gap-ledger)')


def queue_sets(lines):
    """(open, settled, heads): the item numbers open in (b) and (c), those settled in (a) and open nowhere,
    and each list of the queue's head that names its items by number, {label in lower case: numbers}."""
    part, opened, settled, heads = None, set(), set(), {}
    for ln in lines:
        if ln.startswith('## '):
            m = re.match(r'## \((\w)\)', ln)
            part = m.group(1) if m else ('after' if part else None)
            continue
        if part in ('b', 'c'):
            m = re.match(r'(\d+)\. ', ln)
            if m:
                opened.add(int(m.group(1)))
        elif part == 'a':
            m = re.match(r'- \*\*(?:Items? )?(\d+)[,.]', ln)
            if m:
                settled.add(int(m.group(1)))
        elif part is None:
            for m in HEAD_LIST.finditer(ln):
                heads[m.group(1).strip().lower()] = {int(x) for x in re.findall(r'\d+', m.group(2))}
    return opened, settled - opened, heads


def findings_built(rev):
    """{(batch, finding): [(hash, subject)]}: the review findings that a commit in rev's history names,
    for each commit that changes a file outside the record."""
    r = subprocess.run(['git', '-C', a.root, 'log', '--format=%x00%h%x01%s%x01%B%x01', '--name-only', rev],
                       capture_output=True, text=True)
    out = collections.defaultdict(list)
    for chunk in r.stdout.split('\x00')[1:]:
        h, s, body, files = chunk.split('\x01', 3)
        if not [f for f in files.split('\n') if f.strip() and not RECORD.match(f.strip())]:
            continue
        msg = s + '\n' + body
        named = set()
        for m in re.finditer(r'batch-(\w+)-review\.md,? findings? (\d+(?:(?:,\s*|,? and )\d+)*)', msg):
            named.update((m.group(1).lower(), int(n)) for n in re.findall(r'\d+', m.group(2)))
        for m in re.finditer(r"[Cc]limb batch (\w+)'s (?:review, |post-batch review, )?findings? (\d+(?:(?:,\s*|,? and )\d+)*)", msg):
            named.update((m.group(1).lower(), int(n)) for n in re.findall(r'\d+', m.group(2)))
        for k in named:
            out[k].append((h, s))
    return out


def stale(plan, queue, rev):
    """The LOOK lines of PLAN's lines against the queue and the history of rev."""
    opened, settled, heads = queue_sets(queue)
    built = findings_built(rev)
    out, h2, h3 = [], None, None
    for i, ln in enumerate(plan, 1):
        if ln.startswith('## '):
            h2, h3 = ln[3:].strip(), None
            continue
        if ln.startswith('### '):
            h3 = ln[4:].strip()
            continue
        if not ln.lstrip().startswith('- '):
            continue
        why = []
        nums = []
        for m in ITEMS.finditer(ln):
            nums += [int(x) for x in re.findall(r'\d+', m.group(1))]
        own = [int(x) for m in OWN.finditer(ln) for x in re.findall(r'\d+', m.group(1))]
        s = sorted({n for n in nums if n in settled})
        marked = bool(CLEANUP_MARK.search(ln))
        if own and all(n in settled for n in own) and not any(n in opened for n in nums):
            if not marked:
                why.append('settled: its own review-queue item is in (a): %s' % ', '.join(map(str, sorted(set(own)))))
        elif s and len(set(nums)) >= 3:
            why.append('list: it names items in (a) among open ones: %s' % ', '.join(map(str, s)))
        q = re.search(r"the queue's \"([^\"]+)\"", ln)
